examples.vi: Cha mẹ cố gắng dạy những giá trị tốt đẹp cho con cái.

senses.vi: giá trị; tiêu chuẩn

senses.definition: A number or mathematical quantity found by calculating or measuring.

examples.en: Calculate the exact value of x in the equation.
examples.vi: Tính giá trị chính xác của x trong phương trình.

senses.vi: giá trị

thesaurus.definition: a numerical quantity measured or assigned or computed
the quality (positive or negative) that renders something desirable or valuable
the amount (of money or goods or services) that is considered to be a fair equivalent for something else
relative darkness or lightness of a color
(music) the relative duration of a musical note
an ideal accepted by some individual or group

examples: There is tremendous value in a good education.
An abacus is of little value when you have an electronic calculator.
wiktionary.gloss: The quality that renders something desirable or valuable; worth.

examples: The value of my children's happiness is second only to that of my wife.
wiktionary.gloss: The degree of importance given to something.

examples: He does not share his parents' values.
family values
wiktionary.gloss: That which is valued or highly esteemed, such as one's morals, morality, or belief system.

examples: The value of the stolen painting is estimated to be around four million pounds.
wiktionary.gloss: The amount (of money or goods or services) that is considered to be a fair equivalent for something else.

examples: The value of a crotchet is twice that of a quaver.
wiktionary.gloss: The relative duration of a musical note.
The relative darkness or lightness of a color in (a specific area of) a painting etc.

examples: The exact value of pi cannot be represented in decimal notation.
wiktionary.gloss: Any definite numerical quantity or other mathematical object, determined by being measured, computed, or otherwise defined.

examples: the value of a word; the value of a legal instrument
wiktionary.gloss: Precise meaning; import.

examples: The vein carries good values.
the values on the hanging walls
wiktionary.gloss: The valuable ingredients to be obtained by treating a mass or compound; specifically, the precious metals contained in rock, gravel, etc.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English valew, value, from Old French value, feminine past participle of valoir, from Latin valēre (“be strong, be worth”), from Proto-Italic *walēō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂welh₁- (“to be strong”).

senses.definition: To think that someone or something is important, useful, or special.

examples.en: I really value your friendship and honest support.
examples.vi: Tôi thực sự trân trọng tình bạn và sự hỗ trợ chân thành của bạn.

senses.vi: coi trọng; quý trọng; trân trọng

senses.definition: To decide or estimate how much money something is worth.

examples.en: The painting was valued at two million dollars.
examples.vi: Bức tranh được định giá hai triệu đô la.

senses.vi: định giá; đánh giá

thesaurus.definition: fix or determine the value of; assign a value to
hold dear
regard highly; think much of
evaluate or estimate the nature, quality, ability, extent, or significance of
estimate the value of

examples: I will have the family jewels valued by a professional.
The property has been valued at six million pounds.
wiktionary.gloss: To determine or estimate the value of; to judge the worth of.

examples: Gold was valued highly among the Romans.
I value his advice.
wiktionary.gloss: To regard highly; think much of; place importance upon.

examples: I value these old photographs.
wiktionary.gloss: To hold dear; to cherish.

idioms.gloss: Accept as presented, without question or further investigation.
To perform the above-defined action with an amount.
To make a product or service more desirable or useful.
Having features added to a basic line or model for which the buyer is prepared to pay extra.
To bet with the intention of being called in order to extract more money from a likely worse hand.
To raise with the intention of being called in order to extract more money from a likely worse hand.
Synonym of take at face value.
To be aware of one's worth and insist that others respect it, for example by not underpricing one's services.
Used to celebrate the end or demise of someone or something unfavorable or disliked.
idioms.phrase: and nothing of value was lost

known: and nothing of value was lost

tatoeba.en: The overuse of discounts has cheapened the brand's value over time.
tatoeba.vi: Việc lạm dụng giảm giá đã làm giảm giá trị nhãn hàng theo thời gian.

tatoeba.en: The results that you get depend on the values of the parameters that you set.
tatoeba.vi: Kết quả mà bạn nhận được phụ thuộc vào các giá trị tham số mà bạn đặt.

blocks.etymology: Borrowed from French vandalisme, first used by Henri Grégoire to decry the pillage and destruction of art in the course of the French Revolution, in reference to the East Germanic tribe of the Vandals, which looted Rome in 455. By surface analysis, vandal + -ism.

senses.definition: the crime of deliberately damaging or destroying public or private property

examples.en: The phone booth was destroyed in an act of vandalism.
examples.vi: Bốt điện thoại đã bị phá hủy trong một vụ phá hoại của công.

senses.vi: hành vi phá hoại tài sản; tính hay phá hoại

thesaurus.definition: willful wanton and malicious destruction of the property of others

vi_block: Tính hay phá hoại những công trình văn hoá (với ác tâm hay vì ngu dốt).

examples: As we turned down the street I was appalled by the vandalism: spray paint and smashed windows that were everywhere.
wiktionary.gloss: Willful damage to or destruction of any property, such as graffiti or defacement.

blocks.etymology: From Middle French verbosité, from Late Latin verbōsitās. By surface analysis, verbose + -ity.

thesaurus.definition: an expressive style that uses excessive or empty words

vi_block: Tính dài dòng (báo cáo, bài văn... ).

wiktionary.gloss: The excess use of words, especially using more than are needed for clarity or precision.

examples: Mind you don't walk into that wall.
Watch where you're going. You nearly walked into that man.
wiktionary.gloss: To collide with by walking.

examples: The platoon walked into an ambush.
You really walked into that trap, didn't you?
wiktionary.gloss: To fall into (a trap or other situation), especially one that could have been avoided with more care.

blocks.etymology: From water + sport.

wiktionary.gloss: Any sport played on or in water; such as swimming or water skiing.
Synonym of watersports (“sexual practice involving urine”).
